relationships.subject: AM1241
relationships.evidence_quote: administration of the CB2-selective AM1241 (MD 3.94, 95%CI 2.13, 5.75) is associated with increased paw withdrawal thermal latency in male rats

relationships.subject: 2-arachidonoylglycerol
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these findings show that activation of CB1/2 receptors by the endocannabinoids AEA and 2-AG is associated with reduced cancer-induced bone pain in the rodent models described.

relationships.subject: JZL184
relationships.evidence_quote: administration of the monoacylglycerol lipase (MAGL) inhibitor JZL184, which is known to enhance the levels of 2-AG83, reduced paw withdrawal frequency in male mice inoculated with osteolytic sarcoma cells84

relationships.subject: CB2 receptor
relationships.evidence_quote: The CB2-selective agonist JWH-015 also reduced cancer-induced bone pain in rats, and this effect was inhibited by the CB2-selective inverse/agonist AM630, suggesting a CB2 mediated effect91.

key_findings: Meta-analysis: endocannabinoids and synthetic CB1/CB2 agonists reduced pain behaviours in rodent cancer-induced bone pain models.
In humans, delta-9-THC, NIB and medical cannabis reduced cancer pain intensity, with low certainty of evidence.
